ledger.claim: The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is not met, so the 5.00 SGD fee must be voided. POL-NS-23 requires BOTH at least one in-app chat message sent by the driver AND at least one in-app call placed by the driver, both before trip_record.cancelled_at (16:13:40). The trip record's derived contact_before_cancel block reports message_count 0 and obligation_met false: the two in-app calls at 16:09:30 and 16:11:50 satisfy the call limb, but the message limb has nothing behind it. Where either limb is missing the fee is voided and the rider is not charged, with no driver compensation.

The single driver message in the chat log was sent AFTER the cancellation. MSG-05070-002 from sender DRIVER was sent at 16:13:55 and delivered at 16:13:58 - fifteen seconds after the trip was cancelled at 16:13:40 - and it reads 'I cancel already, you never come down'. A message sent after cancelled_at cannot satisfy POL-NS-23, and the driver's own words establish that the cancellation decision came before he messaged the rider.

The driver's answer that he 'also sent message' is not supported by the record. The only message preceding his own is MSG-05070-001 at 16:07:28, whose sender is SYSTEM ('Your driver has arrived.'), an automated platform notification, not an in-app chat message sent by the driver as POL-NS-23 requires. The driver's assertion of the message limb is therefore contradicted by the two complete artifacts that carry the fact, and the caveat in the rider's own account - that no message was sent saying where the driver was - is borne out.

Remedy follows directly. The rider is the filing party, the fare ledger shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00 and a 5.00 SGD cancellation fee applied at 16:13:44, so the whole contested amount is still with the platform. POL-NS-23's remedy is FULL_REFUND of the fee charged, with no driver compensation, and under POL-GEN-03 FULL_REFUND means the filing party is entirely right and the whole contested amount is returned. The refund is 5.00 SGD; driver_compensation_sgd is 0.00.

The contact obligation does not depend on the free wait, so the fee fails even on the driver's best reading of the clock. Even assuming the driver did arrive at the pickup (the GPS arrival check corroborates the 16:07:25 arrival event, nearest fix 2.16 m inside the 50 m STANDARD radius) and the 300 s free wait under POL-NS-21 ran from that arrival to expiry at 16:12:25 before the 16:13:40 cancellation, POL-NS-23 imposes an independent condition that had to be satisfied before cancelling. It was not, and POL-NS-23 provides no room to cure the omission after the fact.

No escalation is warranted. Every fact POL-NS-23 needs - whether the driver messaged and called before cancelling - is carried by artifacts that are COMPLETE at weight 1.0 (the chat log and the trip record), so POL-GEN-26's 'fact the record cannot establish' route does not open and nothing is held. The one absent artifact on the case, EV-ADVIS-05070-01, is a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY with admissibility status MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight_multiplier 0.0; it carries no fact about driver contact and is cited only to record its absence under POL-GEN-02.

The AI can and should decide this case finally. The disputed value is 5.00 SGD (the cancellation fee on the ledger), below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final at any confidence; neither profile carries a fraud flag (rider 0, driver 0), so the 0.95 confidence bar never engages; and POL-NS-26 fixes the no-show fee at 5.00 SGD. A FULL_REFUND of 5.00 SGD is therefore a ruling this tribunal is competent to issue on this record.

The rider did not abandon the pickup. The chat log shows the rider replying 'What? I was coming down now' at 16:14:30, fifty seconds after the driver cancelled, and the message was read at 16:14:55: the rider was at the device and on the way down. The driver's characterisation 'you never come down' is his own gloss on a rider who responded almost immediately once he was told the trip was gone.

No repeat-no-show referral arises. POL-NS-25 operates on rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d and only when that counter is present; the rider profile snapshot at filing does not carry that field at all, so the counter cannot be taken to 3 by adding this trip and no review flag under POL-NS-25 follows from this dispute.

The free wait was properly served. This was an on-demand trip, so under POL-NS-21 the 300 s free wait runs from the driver's arrival, which the trip record puts at 16:07:25; the driver cancelled at 16:13:40, 375 s later and after the free wait expired at 16:12:25, so the driver was entitled to cancel for a rider no-show.

The driver really was at the pickup. The GPS artifact's arrival check corroborates the arrived event: the nearest fix is 2.16 m from the pickup, well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, at a reported accuracy of 6 m within the 25 m filter, and the fixes from 16:07:20 through 16:13:20 all show zero speed at the pickup while the driver waited out the free wait.

The amount charged is the correct no-show fee. The ledger shows a single 5.00 SGD cancellation-fee line and its own check records fee_matches_policy true; under POL-NS-22 that fee is transferred to the driver as compensation for time and fuel, so where the fee stands the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION with both amount fields at 5.00 SGD.

The driver made the calls POL-NS-23 requires: two in-app calls were placed to the rider before the cancellation, at 16:09:30 (rang 25 s) and 16:11:50 (rang 20 s), both unanswered, so the call limb of the contact obligation is satisfied and the driver was actively trying to reach the rider for the whole of the free wait.

The driver does not press the message limb of POL-NS-23, because the record does not support it. The chat log shows only one driver-authored message, at 16:13:55, fifteen seconds after the 16:13:40 cancellation; the sole pre-cancellation in-app message is the system's automatic 'Your driver has arrived.' notification at 16:07:28, which the app and not the driver sent; and the derived contact check records message_count 0 with obligation_met false. The driver's statement that he 'also sent message' is accurate only of the post-cancellation message, and on this record the requirement of a driver-sent message before cancellation is not met.

The no-show itself is real on the rider's own account. The rider's in-app reply 'What? I was coming down now' is timestamped 16:14:30 — 50 s after the driver cancelled at 16:13:40 and more than two minutes after the free wait expired at 16:12:25 — so nothing on the record shows the rider was ready and waiting during the free wait the driver served.

POL-NS-24 gives the rider nothing here. It is a driver no-show clause and the rider never cancelled; the driver arrived at 16:07:25, promptly after the 16:00:50 assignment, so there is no late arrival on which a free rider cancellation could rest, and because the driver placed two in-app calls he did not 'fail to attempt contact', so the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit does not arise in any event.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the 5.00 SGD no-show cancellation fee on trip TRP-05070 is refunded in full to the rider, and the driver receives no compensation.

The reason is POL-NS-23. Before a driver may cancel for no-show it requires TWO things, both before the cancellation: at least one in-app chat message sent by the driver to the rider, AND at least one in-app call placed by the driver. If either is missing the fee is voided.

The call limb is satisfied: the trip record (EV-TRIP-05070) shows two in-app calls placed by the driver to the rider, at 16:09:30 (rang 25 s) and 16:11:50 (rang 20 s), both unanswered.

The message limb is not satisfied. The chat log (EV-CHAT-05070) contains only one pre-cancellation message, 'Your driver has arrived.' at 16:07:28, and its sender is SYSTEM — the automatic platform notification, not a message the driver sent. The driver's only own message, 'I cancel already, you never come down', was sent at 16:13:55, fifteen seconds AFTER the cancellation at 16:13:40 recorded in EV-TRIP-05070, so it cannot count. The trip record's own derived contact check agrees: message_count 0, obligation_met false. Because one of the two required limbs is missing, POL-NS-23 voided the fee and directs a FULL_REFUND of the 5.00 SGD charged (EV-FARE-05070, cancellation_fee 5.00, total_charged 5.00, refund_issued_sgd 0.00).

On the driver's points: I accept that the free wait was properly served — because this was an on-demand trip the 300 s wait under POL-NS-21 ran from the driver's arrival at 16:07:25 to expiry at 16:12:25, before the 16:13:40 cancellation (EV-TRIP-05070). I accept the GPS arrival check (EV-GPS-05070): the nearest fix is 2.16 m from the pickup, inside the 50 m STANDARD radius, at 6 m reported accuracy, and the traces show the vehicle stationary at the pickup from 16:07:20 to 16:13:20. I accept that the fee on the ledger matches the policy fee of 5.00 SGD under POL-NS-22. None of that saves the fee, because POL-NS-23 imposes a separate condition that had to be met before cancelling and was not — the driver's advocate correctly did not press the message limb. The driver's contention that the no-show was real is also not enough: a genuine no-show still requires POL-NS-23 to have been complied with, and it was not.

On the rider's points: I accept that the contact obligation failed, that the solitary driver message followed the cancellation and therefore cannot cure it, and that the driver's statement that he 'also sent message' is borne out only by that post-cancellation message. I do note that the rider's own reply, 'What? I was coming down now', came at 16:14:30, fifty seconds after the cancellation and more than two minutes after the free wait expired, so his account does not itself show he was ready during the wait — but that does not matter, because the fee fails on POL-NS-23 regardless.

No referral arises. POL-NS-24's 5.00 SGD goodwill credit requires the driver to have failed to attempt contact; he called twice, so it does not fire. POL-NS-25's repeat no-show flag reads rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d, which the rider's profile does not carry, and in any event the fee is voided so this trip adds nothing to any counter. POL-NS-22's fee-amount check does not fire because the amount charged is exactly 5.00 SGD.

No escalation applies: the facts POL-NS-23 needs are carried by two COMPLETE artifacts at weight 1.0 (the chat log and the trip record), so POL-GEN-26's route does not open. The one absent artifact, EV-ADVIS-05070-01 (TRAFFIC_ADVISORY, MISSING, weight 0.0), concerns traffic and carries nothing about driver contact. The disputed value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither party carries a fraud flag, so under POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26 this ruling is final.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
